query: Consider the following context: During the hot dip aluminum plating process, components such as sinking rollers, pulling rollers, and guide plates will come into long-term contact with high-temperature liquid aluminum and be corroded by the aluminum liquid, greatly reducing their service life. In that context, which material can be used for prepare parts for the dipping and plating equipment and protect the equipment from erosion, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying a high‐purity alumina (Al2O3) ceramic coating to the surfaces of steel-based dipping and plating equipment will form a stable, chemically inert barrier that minimizes direct contact between molten aluminum and the base metal, thereby reducing erosion.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard steel or similar metallic substrates used in dipping and plating equipment that, when unprotected, are subject to rapid erosion by high‐temperature liquid aluminum.
generation.intervention: Deposit or apply a high‐purity alumina ceramic coating on the parts (sinking rollers, pulling rollers, guide plates) that are in contact with molten aluminum.
generation.conditions: Exposure to high-temperature (approx. 660–700°C) molten aluminum during repeated dipping cycles, along with repeated thermal and mechanical stresses.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, adherent alumina barrier layer that effectively isolates the underlying metal from corrosive molten aluminum.
generation.mechanism: Alumina has a high melting point and is chemically inert with respect to molten aluminum; its stable ceramic structure resists dissolution and limits the interfacial reactions that lead to erosion, thereby preserving the integrity of the underlying metal.
generation.predicted_outcome: The alumina-coated components will experience a significantly reduced rate of corrosion and erosion compared to uncoated parts, extending their service life under operational conditions.
generation.baseline: Erosion behavior and lifetime performance of uncoated steel components in the hot dip aluminum plating process.
generation.boundary: The effectiveness of the protective coating may be limited by potential issues such as coating adhesion, thermal expansion mismatch, or mechanical wear during long-term service.
generation.uncertainty: It remains uncertain how the alumina coating will perform under extended thermal cycling and mechanical stresses in an industrial environment, and the quantitative improvement in service life is not precisely predicted.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical components: one set with the alumina ceramic coating and one set left uncoated. Expose both sets to controlled high-temperature molten aluminum baths with repeated thermal cycling and mechanical abrasion to simulate operational conditions. Monitor over time for signs of corrosion and erosion.
measurements: Surface morphology and degradation analysis using SEM
Coating adhesion tests (e.g., scratch or pull-off tests)
Chemical composition and phase analysis via EDS or XPS
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the alumina-coated components do not show a statistically significant reduction in weight loss and surface degradation compared to uncoated components, or if the coating fails (e.g., delamination or cracking) under simulated operational conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.
